strengths: Well-motivated research question challenging the 'depth = safety' intuition in collaborative inference partitioning
Solid information-theoretic framework with rigorous proofs deriving H(X|Z) lower bounds for feature vs. decision-level representations
Comprehensive experimental validation across four representative architectures (IR-152, ResNet-50, VGG19, ViT) and multiple datasets with consistent findings
Novel analysis of label smoothing effects on representation geometry and R²_c evolution with clear gradient-based derivations
Practical algorithm (Algorithm 1) for automatic Golden Partition Zone localization that is easy to implement
Thorough deployment cost analysis (Appendix I) providing actionable guidance for practitioners on privacy-utility-latency tradeoffs
Excellent experimental design with stress-testing via enhanced inversion models and intermediate information enrichment (Tables 3-4)
Detailed supplementary material including proofs, ablations, and implementation details supporting reproducibility
weaknesses: Limited experimental scope: all images at 64×64 resolution with no evaluation on high-resolution data, language models, or other modalities beyond vision

Theoretical bounds contain loose finite-precision correction terms (κ_Δ) and rely on Gaussian assumptions not empirically validated; gap between bound and empirical 'abrupt' increase not fully explained

Architecture-dependent results significantly limit generalizability: ViT shows no clear GPZ, ResNet delays transition requiring 78% edge-side parameters, suggesting phenomenon is architecture-specific rather than universal principle
Inversion models based on relatively standard architectures; state-of-the-art generative approaches (diffusion-based) less thoroughly evaluated, potentially affecting resistance estimates
Neural Vortex concept explicitly acknowledged as metaphorical rather than a formal mechanism, somewhat weakening novelty of the conceptual contribution
No head-to-head comparison with existing CI defenses (Wang et al., 2022; Xia et al., 2025); authors justify as characterization work, but benchmarking would strengthen claims
Causal relationship between R²_c and MIA resistance is indirect (through bounds on H(X|Z)); R²_c is a consequence of training dynamics rather than direct proxy for privacy
Auxiliary data quality is critical for attack success; strong assumption that attackers have high-quality distribution-matched data may not always hold in practice

strengths: Rigorous information-theoretic analysis with proper differential-to-Shannon entropy bridging and comprehensive proofs
Empirical demonstration that depth alone does not ensure MIA resistance, with concrete counterexamples (e.g., ResNet-50 blocks 25-48 maintaining weak resistance)
Comprehensive experimental evaluation across multiple architectures (IR-152, ResNet-50, VGG19, ViT) and datasets with multiple metrics (MSE, PSNR, SSIM, LPIPS)
Practical deployment cost analysis considering latency, communication, memory, and energy constraints
Stress-testing with enhanced inversion models and representation augmentation strategies demonstrating robustness
weaknesses: Vision Transformer results show oscillatory behavior (Fig. 7) inconsistent with smooth representational transition theory, suggesting framework may not generalize to modern architectures
Theoretical bounds in Eq. (9) are loose with κ_Δ corrections acknowledged as potentially vacuous in absolute value, limiting practical predictive utility despite relative validity
Critical data dependence undermines generalizability: GPZ location shifts substantially across CIFAR-10, FaceScrub, MNIST/KMNIST, requiring per-dataset-model experimentation to locate

R²_c localization method (Algorithm 1) requires manual threshold selection (τ=20%), lacks robustness analysis across training conditions, and provides unclear advantage over simpler deep-split baseline
Absence of quantitative comparison with existing defense mechanisms (noise-based, differential privacy, information-theoretic) makes practical value unclear—is GPZ better than shallow split + noise?
Neural Vortex concept is imprecisely defined as metaphorical explanation rather than formal mechanism, with first-order gradient analysis ignoring momentum, discrete SGD, and learning rate scheduling
Limited actionable deployment guidance: practitioners must still instrument models to find GPZ; unclear when this approach beats simply using deeper splits or existing defenses
Statistical rigor issues: no error bars/significance tests, t-SNE visualizations (Fig. 3) can be misleading, inconsistent label smoothing parameters across experiments (α=0.3 vs -0.05)

strengths: Novel theoretical insight: The paper convincingly demonstrates that representational transition (marked by R²_c contraction), not depth alone, determines MIA resistance. The connection to H(X|Z) through information-theoretic bounds is well-motivated and rigorously derived.

Rigorous theoretical analysis: Careful application of standard lemmas (maximum entropy principle, determinant-trace inequality) with detailed proofs. The treatment of finite-precision effects (Appendix B) and gradient-induced R²_c dynamics (Appendix E) is particularly thorough.

Comprehensive empirical validation: Experiments across 4 representative architectures (IR-152, ResNet-50, VGG19, ViT) and multiple datasets. Multiple evaluation metrics (MSE, PSNR, SSIM, LPIPS) with stress tests using enhanced inversion models and augmented intermediate representations demonstrate robustness.

Practical contributions: Algorithm 1 for automated GPZ location is computationally efficient. Detailed deployment analysis (Appendix I) with latency, communication, and energy tradeoffs provides concrete guidance. Results show 4× higher MSE at GPZ vs. shallow splits, with 66% advantage under enhanced attacks.

Strong empirical consistency: Architecture-specific analysis (ResNets delay, VGG enables early, ViT prevents transitions) reveals how network design affects representational transitions, advancing understanding of privacy-utility tradeoffs.
Well-structured presentation with reproducibility: Comprehensive appendices, detailed hyperparameters, code availability promised. Clear problem motivation and honest discussion of limitations.
weaknesses: Limited scope to vision models: Restricted to images with cautious acknowledgment regarding text domains. Results are architecture-dependent (skip connections delay, persistent tokens prevent transitions), limiting generalizability to modern Transformers and multimodal systems.

Loose information-theoretic bounds: Equation (9) involves multiple layers of inequalities with unknown constants κ_Δ. Authors acknowledge bounds are 'numerically loose,' limiting their utility as quantitative predictive tools. Empirical validation of bound tightness would strengthen claims.

ViT presents counterexample: Figure 7 shows ViT's 6th layer still enables accurate reconstruction despite hypothesis that deeper decision-level representations resist MIA. Persistent patch representations break the feature-vs-decision dichotomy, suggesting theory doesn't universally apply to modern architectures.

Architecture-specific behavior reduces universality: Practitioners need custom analysis for different architectures anyway (ResNet-50 shows dimension expansion can improve MIA despite depth). This diminishes the predictive power of the R²_c criterion as a general guidance principle.

Algorithm 1 design choices lack justification: Dimension normalization and τ=20% threshold appear somewhat arbitrary. Table 5 shows the algorithm produces 'more focused' results than empirical inspection for VGG, suggesting potential brittleness. Sensitivity analysis would strengthen the method.

Limited defense integration: Paper avoids direct comparison with existing defenses. While upstream analysis is valuable, some comparison would clarify complementarity (e.g., does label smoothing independently strengthen partitioning at GPZ?).

Neural Vortex concept is primarily metaphorical: Acknowledged as intuitive flavor rather than formal mechanism. Underlying insights are captured by R²_c analysis; the concept adds interpretability without fundamental new technical depth.

Finite-precision effects underexplored: Thorough Appendix B treatment exists, but implications for main results and sensitivity to different quantization schemes (FP32 vs. INT8) deserve main-text discussion.
